sources.title: Workonline Communications brings African network with global reach to iXAfrica (iXAfrica release, 21 October 2026)
sources.summary: iXAfrica's release datelined 'Nairobi, Kenya, Wednesday October 21, 2026' says Workonline Communications has established a new Point of Presence at iXAfrica Data Centres' NBOX1 campus in Nairobi, bringing its IP backbone into iXAfrica's carrier-neutral ecosystem, and that customers at iXAfrica will be able to access Workonline's IP transit, Ethernet and remote peering services directly from the NBOX1 campus. iXAfrica's chief executive is quoted that the company built NBOX1 as a neutral meeting point where networks, cloud platforms, content providers and enterprises connect, that Workonline brings its network into the campus, and that every network that joins NBOX1 makes the ecosystem more valuable 'for everyone already connected here'. The boilerplate describes a 22.5 MW campus. This is a dated operator statement that NBOX1 is operating with connected customers and networks on 21 October 2026; it is not an opening date and says nothing about NBOX1.2 completion.
sources.date_semantics: Dateline 21 October 2026 in the release text; the post sitemap lastmod is 2026-10-21T11:09:46+03:00 (local ixafrica-post-sitemap1.xml). The page carries no JSON-LD date. Used as the operating-status observation for the NBOX1 campus.

sources.title: iXAfrica: Campus Specs (NBOX1, Mombasa Road, Nairobi)
sources.summary: iXAfrica's campus-specs page describes NBOX1 as situated on a 4.3-acre campus along Nairobi's Mombasa Road, with 17,300 sqm land area, two buildings, 15,587 m2 total footprint and 6,621 m2 colocation space, and full-site IT power of 22.5 MW split as NBOX1.1: 4.5 MW (Live) and NBOX1.2: 18 MW. The site footer gives the address Cabanas, Mombasa Road, Nairobi.
sources.date_semantics: Undated operator page; used only for facility identity, the Mombasa Road location and the phase split (NBOX1.1 live, NBOX1.2 status not stated), not for the status date.

sources.title: Teraco: Johannesburg Data Centres JB1-JB5 (locations page, version modified 28 September 2026)
sources.summary: Teraco's Johannesburg locations page says Teraco operates vendor-neutral colocation data centres in Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban and presents the Isando Campus (JB1 East and West, JB3 and JB5) in Ekurhuleni as the connectivity and interconnection hub that provides the cloud on-ramps for Amazon, Google, Huawei, Microsoft Azure, Oracle and VMware Cloud Verified providers, with an interconnected ecosystem of more than 16,000 cross-connects, 285+ network service providers, 50+ content providers, 160+ IT services providers and 160+ enterprises and financial service providers, direct access to the NAPAfrica internet exchange community, and key attributes of 32,000+ sqm white space and 70 MW IT load. It gives JB1 East & West at 5 Brewery Street, Isando (GPS -26.138000, 28.198020), JB3 at 14 Kiln Road (GPS -26.136132, 28.199605) and JB5 at 29 Kiln Road (GPS -26.135302, 28.201401). It separately lists Bredell JB2 (completed November 2017) and JB4 (completed October 2022) with their own addresses and points.

sources.title: Teraco completes CT2 data centre expansion, increasing Cape Town's hyperscale capacity to 50MW (Teraco release, 10 November 2025)
sources.summary: Teraco's release of 10 November 2025 announces the completion of its CT2 hyperscale data centre expansion in Cape Town, bringing the facility's total critical IT load to 50 MW; the expansion adds 32 MW across eight new data halls over three levels. CT2 is linked by diverse fibre routes to CT1 and the Cape Town campus supports over 7,000 interconnects.
sources.date_semantics: JSON-LD datePublished 2025-11-10 (dateModified 2026-07-17, a site-wide refresh of all posts). Historical identity and capacity context only; outside the 90-day window and not the status date.

sources.title: ODATA: Centros de datos hiperescalables en México (Mexico locations page, Spanish)
sources.summary: ODATA's Mexico locations page says: 'Descubra los centros de datos hiperescalables de ODATA en México ... Nuestros centros de datos combinan una sólida capacidad de energía, conectividad estratégica, una arquitectura de refrigeración de alta eficiencia y operación continua las 24 horas del día, los 7 días de la semana, los 365 días del año. Programa una visita.' It then describes four facilities, each 'Diseñado según el estándar Tier III. Disponibilidad 24/7/365 / Acceso y funcionamiento continuos': QR01 (VYNMSA Parque Industrial Querétaro; 52,350 m2), QR02 (Parque Industrial Amexhe; 22,373 m2), QR03 (Parque Industrial PyME, Los Cues; ODATA's largest Mexican campus; 275,000 m2) and QR04 (Polígono Empresarial San Miguel de Allende, Guanajuato; integrated with QR01-QR03; 15,535 m2).
sources.date_semantics: JSON-LD datePublished 2026-08-15T13:02:51+00:00 and dateModified 2026-09-25T12:49:15+00:00; the odatadc.com page-sitemap lastmod for the Portuguese original (/localidades-mexico/) also reads 2026-09-25T12:49:15. The datePublished is not used: the captured text is the 25 September version, and the August date predates the public relaunch of ODATA's site (the old odatacolocation.com Mexican facility pages dc-qr01, dc-qr03 and es/dc-qr03 were still archived as live 200 pages on 16 and 20 September 2026 - CDX listing queried 23 October 2026, local verifier2-ia-cdx-odatacolocation-mexico-from-202608.json - and the dated 17 September 2026 ODATA/Aligned DeltaFlow release still directs readers to odatacolocation.com). The 25 September modification is bounded by an archived copy: the Internet Archive's only copy of this page's canonical URL (https://odatadc.com/es/ubicaciones-en-M%C3%A9xico/, captured 2026-10-13T22:55:25Z) carries the same datePublished and dateModified and the same facility text, including the 24/7/365 operation statement (source mx-p1-odata-mexico-locations-es-ia-20261013). published_at records the modification day of the captured version; its present-tense description of ODATA's Mexican data centres in continuous 24/7/365 operation, open to visits, is used as a publication-normalised operating observation on 25 September 2026, not an inspection day or opening date. Facility capacities and occupancy are not stated.

sources.title: ODATA Brings Next-Generation Cooling to Latin America with DeltaFlow Liquid Cooling Technology (Aligned Data Centers press release, 17 September 2026)
sources.summary: ODATA announces the deployment of DeltaFlow liquid cooling at two of its flagship campuses, SP04 in Brazil and QR03 in Mexico, supported by a combined US$630 million investment, and says phase-one installation and testing are already underway at both facilities; DeltaFlow units are manufactured in Brazil and the US to supply ODATA's sites in Mexico and Brazil.

sources.summary: Dated Santiago de Querétaro, 30 April 2025: ODATA launches the first facility on its DC QR03 campus in Parque Industrial PyME, Querétaro; the campus will have five buildings on almost 275,000 m2 and up to 300 MW IT; the first building offers 72 MW IT and is readily available; 200 MW were energized in February 2025.
